newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor soars on reserve, production record.
newsitem.headline: Suncor soars on reserve, production record.

text.p: Shares of integrated oil company Suncor Inc soared to a new high on Monday after the company announced reserve replacement and production figures that surpassed many analysts' predictions.
Suncor stock climbed up to 62 in early trade before settling back to 59.65, up 2.65.

The company said on Monday its conventional oil and gas division in 1996 added more than 30 million barrels of oil equivalent for the second straight year and set a new record for production by averaging 38,9000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 18 percent over 1995.
"It beat many of the street expectations, but it fit with my expections," FirstEnergy Capital Corp analyst Martin Molyneaux said.

Barry Stewart, Suncor's group vice-president of exploration and production, said in a statement that the company replaced over 200 percent of its production with proved reserves at C$6 per BOE, its target for finding and development costs.

"Our 1996 results bring our three-year average to C$5.75 per BOE," Stewart said. "Our proved reserve replacement ratio from finding and development has averaged 240 percent during that same time period."
